rows.final_jof_value: Let the forecast-origin information include B, let Y≥B almost surely, and let 0<τ<1. Project any issued report c to max(B,c). Its pinball loss is no larger at every possible Y. A true conditional lower inverse quantile q at level τ=1−α has strict breach probability at most α. Equality is not automatic: an atom at the quantile can make the probability smaller. The lower bound alone need not create an outcome atom; fitted reports do not inherit the population statement.

rows.final_jof_value: Proof. Below B both errors are nonnegative, so their loss difference is the displayed nonnegative quantity; otherwise the report is unchanged. For the conditional inverse quantile, F(q)≥τ, hence the strict-tail probability is at most α. An atom is a possible reason for strict inequality, not a necessary premise. Accordingly, the retained equality-based coverage tests are diagnostics of their stated nulls, not automatic tests of every valid upper quantile.

rows.final_jof_value: Let future real increments be independent and individually symmetric about zero. Write S<sub>h</sub> for their partial sums, S<sub>0</sub>=0, and fix an observed starting position x with B=|x|. No identical-distribution or finite-moment assumption is required. If q is the population (1−α/2) quantile of |S<sub>H</sub>|, the report B+q has strict peak-breach probability at most α. This is a direct scalar application of the classical Lévy maximal inequality, not a new inequality.

rows.final_jof_value: Proof. The triangle inequality gives the first inclusion; Lévy’s maximal inequality and the inverse-quantile tail bound give the rest. For conditional coverage, independence and symmetry must hold conditional on origin information and q must be the corresponding conditional population quantile. The empirical plug-in L, overlapping historical labels and dependent mean-reverting data do not acquire that guarantee. A generic one-sided endpoint VaR is not the required absolute-displacement quantile. Supplement S15 gives an exact finite counterexample to that substitution; Supplement S11 retains the proof, original simulations and corrected sensitivities.

suggested_manuscript_paragraph: A precommitted extension examines whether the short-history pattern transports to the 17 CFTC aggregate dealer-position markets at a six-week horizon. The 52- and 260-week results were already known and are reused unchanged; only the 520-week forecasts were new. Both registered low-history screens pass: QR4 loses to its matched rolling reference in 15 of 17 cells and QR33 in 29 of 34. The high-history QR4 screen fails, because 10 of 17 wins (58.8%) fall below the fixed 60% rule; strict improvement over all three windows holds in only 6 of 17 markets. The primary verdict is therefore partial support. These dependent aggregate-market counts describe transport of a fixed prediction; they do not establish a generally sufficient financial history, a causal estimation-cost mechanism, or dealer-level replication.
suggested_supplement_summary: The archived protocol was committed at 2026-10-26 03:32:15 UTC (effa537bd6d9b89855002aa79f95f62f9ff3761c), before the recorded execution start at 03:32:28.372451 UTC. All 17 markets, the six-candidate penalty menu, H=6, W in {52,260,520}, chronological validation/evaluation split, transported thresholds, and fixed-denominator decision rules were frozen before the new W=520 run. The archive contains 153 complete market/window/method cells, 102 matched conditional comparisons, and 25 counterexample entries with no unknown cells. QR33 has no registered high-region cell, so its high-region prediction is not testable. Separate scalar verification by the same executor reports zero mismatches across 315,512 checks, using absolute 1e-10 plus relative 1e-12 tolerance; it does not repeat the finite-penalty solver fit. The downloaded economic-date vintage does not reconstruct first-release information, and the already inspected W=52/260 outcomes are not prospective confirmations. The summary retains its execution-stage PENDING marker; the dated independent-verification and acceptance receipts carry the completed verification state.
